answer: Coordination Salt Ledger. Every agent action carries a salt derived from a per-identity secret; the ledger admits only one salt per short time window, so many identities cannot act in parallel without collisions. An attacker must acquire and provision distinct salts at a jetty of registration endpoints, each with delay and setup cost. Duplicate or reused salts are rejected. The real expense is the serialized onboarding time per identity, making mass coordination economically slow. A raven flags clusters of correlated salts. This oasis of parallel capacity shrinks as identity count rises.
